items.entity: 2-D rectangular design domain (length L × height H)
items.description: Sec. II.1 and the Fig. 1(a) caption only name a 'Design Domain'. No dimensions or aspect ratio appear anywhere in the text. The 2-D domain is visible only in Figs. 1(a,d), 2(a–c), 3(a,b,d) and A1(b).
readings: L:H = 2:1 (e.g. matching a 2:1:1 3-D cantilever)
L:H = 1.6:1 (as in the 32×20 short-cantilever example of the 99-line code)

items.entity: structured-grid resolution (nelx × nely) and element type
items.description: Element counts are never given. Sites are finite-element cells with one density each (Sec. IV.7; App. A, 'N is the number of elements'). Sec. II.4 and Figs. A1–A3 plot every 2-D site individually, which points to a coarse grid, but the size can only be read off those figures. Element type and shape are not stated either (square bilinear Q4 is the usual assumption).
readings: 20 × 10 elements
32 × 20 elements
40 × 20 elements
60 × 20 elements
60 × 30 elements

items.description: Only 'Fixed Nodes' (Fig. 1a caption) and 'fixed sites/nodes' (Secs. II.1, II.3) are mentioned. The text never says which edge or nodes are fixed, or over what length; this is shown only in Fig. 1(a).
readings: entire left edge, x = 0, 0 ≤ y ≤ H (standard cantilever)
only part of the left edge (e.g. its central 50% of H)
a few discrete nodes on the left edge (e.g. top and bottom corners)

items.entity: fixed nodes – restrained degrees of freedom
items.description: 'Fixed' suggests both in-plane displacement components are zero, but the restrained DOFs are never stated (Fig. 1a caption, Sec. II.1).
readings: clamped: u_x = u_y = 0 at every fixed node
u_x = 0 along the support edge, with u_y restrained at one node only (roller-type)

items.entity: applied force on the free end
items.description: 'Applied Forces' (Fig. 1a caption) and 'load-bearing nodes' (Sec. II.1, Fig. 2c caption) are mentioned, but the text never gives their location, not even that the load sits on the edge opposite the support.
readings: bottom corner of the free (right) edge: x = L, y = 0
mid-height of the free edge: x = L, y = 0.5H
top corner of the free edge: x = L, y = H

items.description: The plural wording 'Applied Forces' / 'load-bearing nodes' (Fig. 1a caption, Sec. II.1) leaves open whether the load is one nodal point load or is spread over several nodes.
readings: single nodal point load
load spread evenly over a few adjacent nodes (short patch ≈0.1H) on the free edge
uniform shear traction over the whole free edge

items.description: The direction is never stated in the text; only the arrows in Fig. 1(a) would show it. 'Cantilever beam' implies a transverse load. Reversing the sign of a single load gives the same layout and compliance.
readings: vertical, downward (−y)
vertical, upward (+y), same result as downward
inclined or horizontal (axial component)

items.description: The load magnitude is not given. Temperatures are quoted 'in units of compliance' (Sec. II.1), so the cited thresholds T ≈ 20.7, 17.2 and 3.3 depend on this normalization.
readings: |F| = 1 (unit load, as in [17])
total |F| = 1 split over the load-bearing nodes
other or physical magnitude

items.description: No passive regions are mentioned. The phrase 'fixed sites' (Secs. II.1, II.3) most likely means elements at the displacement supports, not elements with a fixed density, but this is never said explicitly.
readings: none (all elements designable)
solid non-design elements next to the fixed nodes
solid non-design pad around the load-bearing node(s)

items.entity: volume constraint V_f = 0.5 – which density field it applies to
items.description: V_f = 0.5 is stated (Sec. II.1). Eq. (5) and App. A impose it on the raw particle positions x_e, yet a density filter is used (App. C). It is unclear whether the constraint applies to filtered (physical) or unfiltered densities.
readings: sum of filtered/physical densities = 0.5·N (standard density-filter practice)
sum of raw design variables x_e = 0.5·N (literal reading of Eq. (5) and App. A)

items.description: Neither E0 nor the thickness is given anywhere. Both scale the compliance, and therefore the 'compliance-unit' temperature scale.
readings: E0 = 1, t = 1 (normalized, as in [17])
physical values (e.g. E0 = 210 GPa, t ≠ 1)

items.description: Neither Poisson's ratio nor plane stress vs plane strain is stated anywhere in the text.
readings: ν = 0.3, plane stress (default of the 88/99-line codes)
ν = 0.3, plane strain
other ν (e.g. 0.25 or 1/3), plane stress

items.description: Sites may reach x = 0, 'void' (Secs. II.1, IV.7). A non-singular stiffness matrix needs E_min > 0 or x_min > 0, and no value is given.
readings: modified SIMP, E_min = 1e-9·E0 (88-line code)
classic SIMP with density lower bound x_min = 1e-3 (99-line code)
E_min = 1e-3·E0

items.description: The text says only that higher density lowers compliance (Fig. 1 caption). No interpolation law or penalty exponent is given, either for the sampled solutions or for the reference optimum of Fig. 3a ('as solved by [17]', references removed).
readings: SIMP, p = 3 (default of the 88/99-line codes)
p = 1 (unpenalized, variable-thickness sheet)
continuation p = 1 → 3

items.description: App. C says a density filter was used for the sampled solutions, and the Fig. A3 caption notes a filter–boundary interaction. The Fig. 3a optimum is 'as solved by [17]', and the filter used there is not stated.
readings: density filter with linear cone weights, kernel truncated at the domain boundary
sensitivity filter (99-line default; ft = 1 in the 88-line code)
density filter for the sampled solutions, sensitivity filter for the Fig. 3a optimum

items.description: No filter radius appears anywhere in the text (App. C mentions the density filter only).
readings: r_min = 1.2 elements
r_min = 1.5 elements
r_min = 2.0 elements
r_min = 3.0 elements

items.entity: optimizer, initial design and stopping rule for the deterministic optimum
items.description: Fig. 3a is 'an optimized solution as solved by [17]', with no optimizer, move limit, starting design or convergence criterion given. Sec. III says conventional topology optimization is the zero-temperature limit of the molecular-dynamics sampling.
readings: OC (move 0.2, damping 0.5), uniform start x = 0.5, stop when max |Δx| < 0.01 (defaults of [17])
MMA with a fixed iteration budget
annealing the Nosé–Hoover sampling to T → 0 from a uniform or random start

items.description: Sec. IV.1 defines compliance as the integral of the strain-energy density (= ½ uᵀKu). The usual compliance in [17] is Fᵀu = uᵀKu, twice that. This changes C values and the 'compliance-unit' temperatures, not the layout.
readings: C = Fᵀu = uᵀKu (standard)
C = ½ uᵀKu (literal reading of Sec. IV.1)

items.description: Not given: thermostat type ('Nosé–Hoover' in Sec. II.1 vs 'Nosé–Hoover chain' in App. A), chain length (written N_c, N_x and M in App. A), Nosé masses Q_k, time step, temperature grid, and equilibration and sampling lengths. These are needed only to reproduce Figs. 1(d), 2 and 4, not the zero-temperature optimum.
readings: not needed: solve only the deterministic minimum-compliance problem
single Nosé–Hoover thermostat (N_c = 1), as worded in Sec. II.1
Nosé–Hoover chain with N_c = 3–5 (common default), as in App. A
temperature sweep ≈ 0–25 compliance units (values cited in Sec. II.1 and Fig. 4)

locator: Sec. II.1, the 2-D cantilever of Fig. 1
